label: About
title: About The Mirror Held Above the Pile
short_blurb: A daily generated front page where the image is the interface.
body: Daily Frontpage is a daily generated interactive front page. Each edition starts from a saved source, becomes a new image-led scene, and stays explorable in the archive. The image is the interface: a visible mark in the scene opens the real source that shaped the day.

This edition began with one saved post, @bywillak: Flat No More. Its image from pbs.twimg.com set the palette, contrast, edge behavior, and gesture. The scene became The Mirror Held Above the Pile: Lacquered cartoon pileup on flat cobalt blue, horizontal frieze procession: the heap unstacked into a low sliding parade along a diagonal sage-cream wavy-striped ramp, toothy puddle-mouths ringed in yellow on a tilted pink floor, a fanged black-red zigzag mouth gripping the far left corner. High in open blue, two pi... After the image was made, a plate-reading pass mapped the source to Pink raised hands lifting gold-rimmed oval collage-face mirror.

typography.rationale: Fraunces and Newsreader fit image-led art objects while Space Grotesk keeps process labels crisp.
